Requirement: PR description and `docs/plans/issue-5927-bound-plain-mode-hold-plan.md` Tests section: "A hold whose `created_at` is missing or unparseable → `blocked`." Also: the new code's "or one whose time cannot be read" branch in `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:280` and the module docstring at lines 51-59 promise a hand-back for any undatable input.
Expected change site: `tests/test_check_in_status.py::test_hold_with_an_unreadable_time_is_handed_back` (lines 1070-1080).
Evidence of absence: The test parametrizes only `[None, "", "not-a-time", 12345]`. None of these inputs reaches the `TypeError` path in `_hours_since` that is documented under the "or one whose time cannot be read" branch. `None` and `""` short-circuit the `isinstance` / `not value` guards in `_hours_since`; `12345` fails `isinstance(value, str)`; `"not-a-time"` raises `ValueError` from `fromisoformat`. A timezone-less ISO timestamp such as `"2026-09-22T12:00:00"` is the only shape that produces a naive `datetime` and triggers the uncaught `TypeError`, and it is not in the parametrize list. The test passes against the buggy code, so the bug can ship undetected and resurface later.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
Requirement: PR description and the new code's intent: a hold at least `CLAUDE_FIX_HOLD_MAX_HOURS` old, or one whose comment time cannot be read, reports `state: blocked` so the bounded blocked-PR intervention can run. The new `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py:280-288` reads `hold_claim.get("at")` through `_hours_since`, which is supposed to map every undatable input to `None` so the caller can fall through to the unknown-age / blocked branch.
Expected change site: `workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/check_in_status.py::_hours_since` (lines 612-618) and the parallel try/except in `read_fix_claims` (line 605).
Evidence of absence: `_hours_since` catches only `ValueError`. For a syntactically valid timezone-less ISO timestamp, `_parse_time` returns a naive `datetime`, the subtraction raises `TypeError`, and the helper does not return `None` — it propagates. The same pattern is in `read_fix_claims`. The contract the PR describes ("or one whose time cannot be read, reports `state: blocked`") is therefore not satisfied for the timezone-less case. A minimal fix is to catch `(TypeError, ValueError)` in both spots, or to make `_parse_time` treat a naive parsed value as UTC.
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
